00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:11.720: A sustained, resonant bell tone, low-pitched and slowly decaying, fills the audio space. No speech, clicks, or other sounds are present.

00:00:11.720 --> 00:00:12.500: The bell tone ends abruptly. A male voice begins speaking, clear and measured: “What is Nirvana?”

00:00:12.500 --> 00:00:28.000: The same male voice continues: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.”

00:00:28.000 --> 00:00:40.000: The male voice continues: “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:00:40.000 --> 00:00:43.000: A brief pause. No speech. No other sounds.

00:00:43.000 --> 00:00:46.000: A different male voice, slightly lower in pitch and with a different cadence, asks: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:00:46.000 --> 00:01:08.000: The second male voice continues: “You do not see Nirvana right now, because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there. What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things. Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:01:08.000 --> 00:01:20.000: The second male voice continues: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:01:20.000 --> 00:01:22.000: A brief pause. No speech. No other sounds.

00:01:22.000 --> 00:01:24.000: The first male voice returns, asking: “What keeps it going?”

00:01:24.000 --> 00:01:36.000: The first male voice continues: “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored. What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst. Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.”

00:01:38.000 --> 00:01:40.000: The second male voice asks: “How is the sense of self constructed?”

00:00–00:02: A sustained, high-pitched electronic tone, pure sine wave, centered in the stereo field, no speech, no background noise.

00:02–00:10: A male voice begins speaking, clear and resonant, with slight room reverb. “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.”

00:10–00:20: The same male voice continues, slightly slower, with deliberate pacing. “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:20–00:30: The voice shifts slightly in tone — more analytical, perhaps slightly faster. “There seems to be some contradiction in the commentarial definitions of nibbana. On the one hand we have the definition of nibbana as the exit from craving which is called ‘awakening’…”

00:30–00:40: Voice continues, with a slight rise in inflection on “on the other.” “...and on the other it is said that it is on seeing nibbana the craving is destroyed. To project nibbana into a distance and to hope that craving will be destroyed only on seeing it is something like trying to build a staircase to a palace one cannot yet see.”

00:40–00:48: Voice becomes more measured, almost academic. “In fact, this is a simile in which the Buddha had used in his criticism of the Brahmins’ point of view.”

00:48–00:58: Voice shifts to a more formal, almost recitative tone, with a slight pause before quoting. “In the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta we have a very clear statement of the third noble truth. Having first said that the second noble truth is craving, the Buddha goes on to define the third noble truth in these words: ‘Tassa yeva tanhāyā asesā virāgā nirodho.’”

00:58–01:00: The voice ends abruptly. No fade-out, no trailing echo. Immediate silence.
